name: apply: each call has its own parameters while a lambda passed to it runs
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => f(x) + x; apply(y => apply(z => z, y + 10), 1)

name: apply: the calls in progress reach a depth of 4
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => f(x) + x; apply(y => apply(z => z, y + 10), 1)

name: apply: depth-exceeded at a depth limit of 3
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => f(x) + x; apply(y => apply(z => z, y + 10), 1)

diagnostics.message: calls and nested values went deeper than the depth limit of 3

name: steps: a lambda written at a parameter with a function type charges 1 where it stands
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => f(x); apply(x => x, 1)

name: steps: the name of a const-bound lambda charges nothing where it stands
source: const id = x => x; const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => f(x); apply(id, 1)

name: steps: a parameter with a function type passed on charges nothing where it stands
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => f(x); const pass = (g: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => apply(g, x); pass(x => x, 1)

name: steps: a parameter with a function type given to map charges nothing where it stands
source: const g = (f: (x: int) => int): int[] => [1, 2, 3].map(f); g(x => x * 10)

name: steps: the step limit falls in the lambda passed
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => f(x) + x; apply(y => apply(z => z, y + 10), 1)

diagnostics.message: the run needed more than its limit of 9 steps

name: steps: the step limit is not reached at 10
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => f(x) + x; apply(y => apply(z => z, y + 10), 1)

name: sumBy: a helper that takes a function
source: type Order = {qty: int, price: float}; const sumBy = (xs: Order[], f: (o: Order) => float): float => xs.map(f).sum(); sumBy(orders, o => o.qty * o.price)

name: a parameter with a function type passed on twice
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => f(x); const twice = (g: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => apply(g, apply(g, x)); twice(n => n * 3, 2)

name: a lambda with fewer parameters drops the extra arguments
source: const two = (f: (a: int, b: int) => int): int => f(1, 2); [two(a => a * 10), two((a, b) => a + b), two(() => 7)]

name: a lambda with a default at a parameter with a function type
source: const call = (f: (x: int | null) => int, x: int | null): int => f(x); [call((x = 5) => x * 2, null), call((x = 5) => x * 2, 1)]

name: a lambda with a pattern at a parameter with a function type
source: const call = (f: (p: {a: int, b: int}) => int): int => f({a: 2, b: 3}); call(({a, b}) => a * b)

name: a typed const-bound lambda named at a parameter with a function type
source: const dbl = (x: int): int => x * 2; const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => f(x); apply(dbl, 4)

name: a lambda passed reads the names of the call where it was written
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => f(x); const adder = (n: int): int[] => [1, 2].map(x => apply(y => y + n, x)); [adder(10), adder(20)]

name: a chain of lambdas passed to calls of its own name
source: const r = (f: (x: int) => int, n: int): int => n == 0 ? f(0) : r(y => f(y) + n, n - 1); r(x => x, 3)

name: filter with a parameter whose result is unknown
source: const keep = (xs: int[], p: (x: int) => unknown): int[] => xs.filter(p); keep([1, 2, 3, 4], x => x % 2 == 0)

name: reduce with a parameter with a function type
source: const fold = (xs: int[], f: (a: int, b: int) => int): int => xs.reduce(f, 0); fold([1, 2, 3], (a, b) => a + b)

name: walk with a parameter with a function type
source: const nodes = (root: any, kids: (n: any) => any): any[] => walk(root, kids); nodes(t, x => x.kids).map(x => x.n)

name: sortBy with a parameter with a function type
source: const by = (xs: string[], key: (s: string) => int): string[] => xs.sortBy(key); by(["ccc", "a", "bb"], s => len(s))

name: the call of a parameter with a function type whose result is unknown
source: const test = (p: (x: int) => unknown, x: int): bool => p(x) ? true : false; [test(x => x > 1, 2), test(x => x == 0, 2)]

name: depth: a call of a parameter with a function type adds 1 plus its nesting depth
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => f(x); apply(x => x, 1)

name: depth: a call on the right of + adds 2
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => 0 + f(x); apply(x => x, 1)

diagnostics.message: calls and nested values went deeper than the depth limit of 2

name: depth: a call on the right of + runs with a depth limit of 3
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => 0 + f(x); apply(x => x, 1)

name: depth: given to map, the library call's measure
source: const g = (f: (x: int) => int): int[] => [1].map(f); g(x => x)

name: depth: a recursion through a parameter with a function type reaches the default limit: 198 calls of r, and f(0) adds 2
source: const r = (f: (x: int) => int, n: int): int => n == 0 ? f(0) : r(f, n - 1); r(x => x + 1, 197)

name: depth: a recursion through a parameter with a function type passes the default limit
source: const r = (f: (x: int) => int, n: int): int => n == 0 ? f(0) : r(f, n - 1); r(x => x + 1, 198)

diagnostics.message: calls and nested values went deeper than the depth limit of 200

name: a failure in the lambda passed: its trace
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => f(x) + x; apply(y => [y][3], 1)

diagnostics.message: index 3 is outside the list of length 1

name: a failure in the lambda passed, through map: its trace
source: const g = (f: (x: int) => int): int[] => [1, 2].map(f); g(y => [0, 1][y])

diagnostics.message: index 2 is outside the list of length 2

name: a failure caught in the lambda that called it
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => try { f(x) } catch { x * 100 }; apply(y => fail("no"), 2) + apply(y => y, 3)

name: a failure caught: the caller's names keep their values
source: const r = (f: (x: int) => int, n: int): int => n == 0 ? f(0) : try { r(y => fail("x"), n - 1) } catch { n * 10 + f(n) }; r(y => y + 1, 2)

name: compiled without the type rules: a lambda passed runs on the values it is given
source: const apply = (f: (x: int) => int, x: int): int => f(x); apply(x => x + "!", "a")

name: compiled without the type rules: the shape test counts the parameters of the function type
source: const g = (f: (a: int, b: int, c: int) => int): int[] => [1].map(f); g((a, b, c) => a)

diagnostics.message: the function given to method map has more than 2 parameters

name: compiled without the type rules: a parameter with a function type is a lambda at a parameter that takes a value
source: const g = (f: (x: int) => int): string => "ab".repeat(f); g(x => x)

diagnostics.message: argument 1 of method repeat cannot be a function

name: compiled without the type rules: map on a value of another kind
source: const g = (f: (x: int) => int): any => t.map(f); g(x => x)

diagnostics.message: a value of kind number has no method map
